html:
A Greek thinker born on the island of Samos around 570 BCE, who founded a community of followers at Croton in southern Italy. He wrote nothing, and most of what we know was written long after his death, often mixed with legend.

He left Samos around 530 BCE, perhaps to escape the tyrant Polycrates. At Croton his followers lived by strict rules about food, dress and silence, and believed the soul is reborn in new bodies, even animals. He is linked with the discovery that musical harmonies follow simple number ratios, and with the idea that number lies behind the order of the world. The theorem named after him was known much earlier in Babylon, and its proof may be later.

His followers became a power in Croton; one of them, the wrestler Milo, led the army that destroyed Sybaris. A backlash later drove the group out, and Pythagoras died at Metapontum. Through Pythagoreanism his ideas shaped Plato and the long tradition of mathematics as a key to nature.
